examples.en: I hung a picture on the white wall.

examples.ko: 이 방은 전체가 백색으로 칠해져 있어요.
examples.en: This whole room is painted white.
White powder was left at the bottom of the cup.

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 거리가 온통 백색이 되었어요.
examples.en: When it snowed, the street turned completely white.

examples.ko: 아이가 백색을 좋아해서 흰 옷만 골라요.
examples.en: My child likes white and only picks white clothes.

examples.ko: 이 컵은 백색인데 저 컵은 파란색이에요.
examples.en: This cup is white, but that cup is blue.

explain: 백색은 한자어라서 글이나 설명에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '흰색'이나 '하얀색'이라고 해요. '백색 가전', '백색 소음'처럼 굳은 말 안에서는 백색이 그대로 나와요.
explain_en: Baeksaek is a Sino-Korean word used in writing and explanations; in everyday talk people say 'huinsaek' or 'hayansaek'. It stays as is in fixed terms like 'baeksaek gajeon' (white goods) and 'baeksaek soeum' (white noise).

examples.ko: 텔레비전 안테나가 부러져서 화면이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The TV antenna is broken, so there is no picture.
My father put an antenna on the roof.
A bird is sitting on the antenna.

examples.ko: 라디오 안테나는 길게 뽑아야 잘 잡혀요.
examples.en: You have to pull the radio antenna out long to get a good signal.
When I changed the direction of the antenna, I could hear the sound.
A robot shaped like an antenna is cute.

explain: 텔레비전이나 라디오 같은 기계에 달아 신호를 받는 장치예요. 휴대폰이 신호를 못 잡을 때는 '신호가 안 잡혀요', '안 터져요'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 새로운 소식이 없는지 안테나를 세우고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm keeping my antenna up for any new news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보나 소문에 민감하게 귀를 기울일 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative expression for staying alert to news or rumors.

explain_en: It is a device attached to machines such as TVs and radios to receive signals. When a phone cannot get reception, people say '신호가 안 잡혀요' or '안 터져요'.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때부터 엘리트 교육을 받았어요.
examples.en: He received an elite education from a young age.
My friend grew up as one of the elite, but is always humble.

examples.ko: 이 회사에는 엘리트들이 많이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Many elites are gathered at this company.
People call that person an elite.

examples.ko: 엘리트가 아니어도 열심히 하면 꿈을 이룰 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if you are not an elite, you can achieve your dream if you work hard.
He teaches at a school that trains elites.

explain: '엘리트 코스', '엘리트 선수'처럼 뒤에 다른 말을 붙여 써요. 칭찬으로 들릴 때도 있고 거리감이 느껴질 때도 있어서 말투에 따라 느낌이 달라져요.
explain_en: It combines with other words, as in 'elite course' or 'elite athlete'. It can sound like praise or sound distant, depending on the tone.

en: move into (a new apartment or building)

examples.en: I move into a new apartment next month.
Our family moved in last week.
I went today to see the house I will move into.
I greeted the neighbor who just moved in.
Once the date is set, I want to move in right away.
The construction was delayed, so we could not move in.

explain: 입주하다는 새로 지은 아파트나 오피스텔처럼 새 건물에 들어갈 때 어울려요. 보통 집에서 집으로 옮길 때는 '이사하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Ipjuhada fits when you move into a newly built apartment or office-tel. When you just move from one home to another, 'isahada' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I fell in front of everyone and it was embarrassing.

examples.ko: 그런 말을 한 게 지금도 창피스러워요.
examples.en: I am still embarrassed that I said something like that.
I made an embarrassing mistake again.

examples.ko: 시험을 못 본 게 창피스럽지 않아요.
examples.en: I am not ashamed that I did badly on the test.

examples.ko: 창피스럽고 속상해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was embarrassed and upset, so I could not say anything.
My face turns red when I am embarrassed.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '창피하다'와 '부끄럽다'가 있어요. '창피하다'는 남이 보는 앞에서 체면이 상할 때, '부끄럽다'는 스스로 느끼는 마음에도 써요. 이 단어는 'ㅂ'이 '워'로 바뀌어서 '창피스러워요'가 돼요.
explain_en: Similar words are 'changpihada' and 'bukkeureopda'. 'Changpihada' is for losing face in front of others; 'bukkeureopda' can also describe a feeling you have about yourself. This word changes ㅂ to 워: 'changpiseureowoyo'.

examples.ko: 우승 트로피를 두 손으로 들어 올렸어요.
examples.en: He lifted the winner's trophy with both hands.
There is a trophy on the bookshelf.
The player's name is engraved on the trophy.
I polish the trophy until it shines and keep it.
I received a trophy and a certificate together.
Even a small trophy is precious to me.

explain: 상을 받을 때 종이는 '상장', 돈은 '상금', 컵이나 조각 모양 물건은 '트로피'라고 따로 불러요. 보통 '트로피를 들어 올리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: When you win a prize, the paper is a 'sangjang', the money is 'sanggeum', and the cup or statue is a 'trophy'. People usually say 'teuropireul deureo ollida' (lift the trophy).

examples.en: I went to the memorial hall with my family on the weekend.
There are many old photos inside the memorial hall.
This memorial hall has no admission fee.
The guide slowly explained the memorial hall to us.

examples.ko: 학교 근처에 새로 생긴 기념관이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a newly opened memorial hall near the school.
I am waiting for the bus to the memorial hall.

explain: '세종대왕기념관'처럼 사람이나 사건 이름 뒤에 붙여요. 여러 종류의 물건을 모아 보여 주는 곳은 보통 '박물관'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It attaches to the name of a person or event, as in 'Sejong the Great Memorial Hall'. A place that shows many kinds of objects is usually called a 'bakmulgwan' (museum).

examples.en: I spread the yoga mat on the floor.
There is a mat laid in front of the entrance.
The children run and play on the mat.
Water got on the mat, so I washed it.
A thin mat fits right into a bag.
It is much more comfortable since I changed to a new mat.

explain: 침대에 쓰는 두꺼운 것은 '매트리스'라고 해요. '매트'는 요가 매트, 현관 매트처럼 바닥에 까는 얇은 것을 가리켜요.
explain_en: The thick one for a bed is a 'maeteuriseu' (mattress). 'Maeteu' means a thin mat laid on the floor, like a yoga mat or an entrance mat.

examples.en: This cafe has a modern interior.
I bought a chair with a modern design.
I want to decorate my room in a modern style.
It is so modern that it looks a bit cold.
It is a modern and neat house.
The building that used to look modern looks old now.

explain: 모던하다는 디자인, 인테리어, 옷처럼 취향을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 말 '현대적이다'는 더 딱딱해서 글에 어울려요.
explain_en: Modeonhada is used for taste in design, interiors, and clothes. The similar 'hyeondaejeogida' is stiffer and suits writing.

examples.en: The alien in the movie came to Earth.
Do aliens live somewhere in space too?
Is there anyone who has seen an alien?
The child drew a picture of an alien.
He wore strange clothes like an alien.
I read a story about becoming friends with an alien.

explain: '외국인'과 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 외국인은 다른 나라에서 온 사람이고, 외계인은 지구 밖에서 온 존재예요.
explain_en: It sounds close to 'oegugin' (foreigner), so learners mix them up. A 'oegugin' is a person from another country; an 'oegyein' is a being from outside Earth.

examples.en: I saw a turtle at the zoo.
A turtle walks slowly.
Tortoises are animals that live a long time.
The child slept hugging a toy turtle.
The tortoise and the hare had a race.
I fed the turtle at the beach.

explain: '거북이'라는 말도 같이 써요. 아주 느린 걸음을 비유할 때는 '거북이걸음'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The form 'geobugi' is also used. A very slow pace is described figuratively as 'geobugigeoreum' (turtle walk).

examples.en: My grandfather collects old records.
I like the warm sound of records.
Dust has piled up on the record.
I saw a record spinning for the first time.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 레코드는 이제 구하기 어려워요.
examples.en: That singer's records are hard to find now.
I played music for my friend on a record.

explain: '레코드판'이라고도 하고 'LP'라고 부르기도 해요. 인터넷으로 듣는 음악은 '음원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is also called 'rekodeupan' or 'LP'. Music you listen to online is called 'eumwon'.

examples.en: I tried to find constellations in the night sky.
My star sign is Pisces.

examples.ko: 별자리가 잘 보이는 곳으로 캠핑 갔어요.
examples.en: We went camping where the constellations are easy to see.
I checked my horoscope with a friend.
The stories about constellations are fun.
In the old days, people told direction by the constellations.

explain: '무슨 별자리예요?'는 하늘의 별이 아니라 생일로 정해지는 별자리를 묻는 말로 나와요. 운세 이야기를 할 때 많이 물어요.
explain_en: 'Museun byeoljariyeyo?' asks your star sign, which is set by your birthday, not a pattern in the sky. It comes up when people talk about horoscopes.

examples.en: I stuck a note on the fridge with a magnet.
The magnet pulls the nails.
The child is playing with a magnet.
Magnets push each other away when the same poles face.

examples.ko: 문 옆 자석에 열쇠를 붙여 둬요.
examples.en: I stick my keys on the magnet next to the door.
That shop draws people like a magnet.

explain: '자석처럼 끌리다'라고 하면 사람이나 장소에 마음이 저절로 끌린다는 비유가 돼요. 냉장고에 붙이는 기념품은 '냉장고 자석'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 'Jaseokcheoreom kkeullida' is a figure of speech for being drawn to a person or place. A souvenir you stick on the fridge is a 'naengjanggo jaseok'.

examples.en: I received a ruby ring as a gift.
A ruby is a red gem.
A ruby is set in my grandmother's necklace.
The sunset was red like a ruby.
It sparkles more when I wipe the ruby with a cloth.
Which do you like, ruby or diamond?

explain: 탄생석 이야기를 할 때 '7월은 루비'처럼 말해요. 붉은 보석이라서 '루비색'이라고 하면 진한 붉은색을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In talk about birthstones, people say 'July is ruby'. Because it is a red gem, 'rubisaek' points to a deep red color.

examples.en: I smoothed the clothes with a steam iron.
Steam comes out, so the room is warm.
When I turn on the steam, my face gets moist.
Dumplings cooked in steam are soft.
I am careful not to burn my hand on the steam.

examples.ko: 스팀 때문에 욕실 거울이 뿌옇게 됐어요.
examples.en: The bathroom mirror fogged up because of the steam.

explain: '스팀 다리미', '스팀 청소기'처럼 가전 이름에 들어가요. '스팀 난방'처럼 증기로 방을 덥히는 난방도 가리켜요. 뜨거운 물에서 나는 김은 그냥 '김'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It appears in appliance names like 'steam iron' and 'steam cleaner'. It also refers to heating that warms a room with steam, as in '스팀 난방'. The vapor from hot water is also simply called '김'.

examples.ko: 아날로그 시계는 바늘로 시간을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: An analog clock shows the time with hands.
Analog things have been catching the eye again lately.

examples.ko: 저는 종이 일기장 같은 아날로그를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like analog things, like a paper diary.
Music feels different when you listen to it in analog.
Please explain the difference between digital and analog.
My father uses an analog-style camera.

explain: 보통 '디지털'과 짝으로 써요. '아날로그 감성'은 손으로 만지는 옛날 물건의 따뜻한 느낌을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually paired with 'digital'. 'Analog gamseong' (analog sensibility) is used for the warm feel of old, hands-on things.

examples.en: I got a silver bracelet as a birthday gift.
The bracelet fits my wrist just right.
A name is engraved on the bracelet.

examples.ko: 팔찌는 손목에 차고 반지는 손가락에 껴요.
examples.en: You wear a bracelet on the wrist and a ring on the finger.
I want to buy a bracelet too.
I bought a bracelet and necklace as a set.

explain: 팔찌는 '차다'나 '하다'와 같이 써서 '팔찌를 차다'라고 말해요. 반지는 '끼다'를 써서 동사가 달라요.
explain_en: A bracelet goes with 'chada' or 'hada': 'paljjireul chada'. A ring uses 'kkida', so the verb is different.

examples.en: I watched the movie in high-definition video.
This camera shoots in high quality.
It is high-definition, so the face is clear.
To watch high quality, your internet has to be fast.
High-resolution photos have large files.
High quality is nice, but I worry about the storage.

explain: 반대말은 '저화질'이에요. 일상에서는 '화질이 좋아요', '화질이 안 좋아요'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is 'jeohwajil'. In daily talk people also say 'hwajiri joayo' (the picture quality is good) or 'hwajiri an joayo'.

examples.en: I do exercises in the park every morning.
Yesterday I got up and did light exercises.
If you do warm-up exercises before working out, your body loosens up.
The children doing exercises are cute.
My grandmother turns on the radio and does exercises.
Tomorrow I will get up early and do exercises.

explain: '체조'는 올림픽 종목이기도 하고 가볍게 몸을 푸는 맨손 운동이기도 해요. 종목을 하는 사람은 '체조 선수'라고 불러요.
explain_en: '체조' is both an Olympic sport and a light bodyweight exercise to loosen up. A person who competes in the sport is called a '체조 선수'.

examples.en: I had a small quarrel with a friend.

examples.ko: 다툼 때문에 하루 종일 기분이 안 좋았어요.
examples.en: I was in a bad mood all day because of the quarrel.
We ended the quarrel and apologized to each other.
Even between a couple there are quarrels.
The police came because of the dispute with a neighbor.
Let us stop talking before it turns into a quarrel.

explain: '다투다'의 명사형이에요. 말이나 의견으로 맞설 때 어울리고, 몸으로 치고받는 일은 보통 '싸움'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the noun form of 'datuda'. It fits a clash of words or opinions; a physical fight is usually called 'ssaum'.

examples.en: An eagle draws a big circle in the sky.
Eagles have very good eyesight.
I saw an eagle for the first time at the zoo.
I want to fly high like an eagle.
Please do not feed the eagle.

examples.ko: 산 위로 독수리 한 마리가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: An eagle flew over the mountain.

explain: 일상에서는 영어 eagle처럼 두루 쓰지만, 새 이름으로는 죽은 동물을 먹는 vulture에 가까워요. 비슷한 큰 새로 '매'와 '수리'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 아직 독수리 타법으로 글을 써요.
phrases.en: typing slowly with one or two fingers
phrases.nuance_ko: 자판을 손가락 한두 개로 찾아 치는 모습을 농담처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking way to describe hunting for keys and typing with one or two fingers.

explain_en: In daily talk it is used broadly like 'eagle', but as a bird name it is closer to a vulture that eats dead animals. Similar big birds are 'mae' (hawk/falcon) and 'suri' (eagle).

examples.en: I was shocked by the sudden news.
I could not speak for a while because of the shock.
That accident was a shock to everyone.

examples.ko: 쇼크가 너무 커서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The shock is so big that I cannot sleep.
He was taken to the hospital in a state of shock.
It takes time to get over the shock.

explain: 마음의 충격은 '충격'과 비슷하게 '쇼크를 받다', '충격을 받다'라고 해요. '쇼크 상태'는 몸에 생기는 의학 용어로도 써요.
explain_en: For mental impact, 'shock' works much like 'chunggyeok': 'syokeureul batda' and 'chunggyeogeul batda'. 'Syokeu sangtae' is also a medical term for a physical state.

examples.en: I collect aluminium cans separately and throw them out.
This pot is made of aluminium.
Aluminium was used for the bicycle frame.
Aluminium is light and does not rust easily.
Cans are made of aluminium and iron.
Aluminium can be recycled too.

explain: 음식을 싸는 얇은 종이 같은 것은 '은박지' 또는 '호일'이라고 해요. 알루미늄은 재료 이름이라 '알루미늄 캔'처럼 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: The thin sheet for wrapping food is called 'eunbakji' or 'hoil'. Aluminium is a material name, so it comes before an object name, as in 'aluminium can'.

en: forget for a moment; slip one's mind

examples.en: I am sorry, I forgot our appointment.
I forgot my umbrella and just came out.
I forgot where I put my keys.
I will write a note so I do not forget again.
I have been forgetting things more lately.
Sometimes I forget my password.

explain: '잊어버리다'보다 가볍게, 잠깐 놓쳤다는 느낌으로 써요. '깜빡 잊었어요', '깜빡했어요' 둘 다 말해요. 눈을 '깜빡이다'와 소리가 비슷하지만 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: It feels lighter than 'ijeobeorida': you just missed it for a moment. People say both 'kkamppak ijeosseoyo' and 'kkamppakaesseoyo'. It sounds close to 'kkamppagida' (to blink) but means something different.

examples.ko: 두 번째 넘버를 부를 때 박수가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was applause when they sang the second number.
A big number is written on the uniform.
I want to be number one.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 제가 제일 좋아하는 넘버예요.
examples.en: This is my favorite number.
We found the owner by the car number.
Musical numbers are easy to memorize.

explain: 일반적으로 숫자를 말할 때는 '번호'를 써요. '넘버'는 '넘버 원', '뮤지컬 넘버'처럼 외래어 표현 안에서 써요.
explain_en: For a plain number, use 'beonho'. 'Neombeo' appears inside loanword expressions like 'number one' and 'musical number'.

examples.en: I have had a rival since school.
Those two are eternal rivals.
Thanks to my rival, I studied harder.
I practice every day to beat my rival.
We ended the match by shaking hands with my rival.

examples.ko: 라이벌은 적이 아니라 힘이 되는 사람이에요.
examples.en: A rival is not an enemy but someone who gives you strength.

explain: '경쟁자'는 일반적인 말이고, '라이벌'은 실력이 비슷해서 서로 의식하는 상대에게 써요. 사이가 나쁘다는 뜻은 아니에요.
explain_en: 'Gyeongjaengja' (competitor) is the general word; 'raibeol' is for an opponent of similar skill whom you keep an eye on. It does not mean the relationship is bad.

examples.en: The celebrity's scandal was in the news.
That politician stepped down because of the scandal.

examples.ko: 스캔들에 대해 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: He said nothing about the scandal.
The company tried to hide the scandal.
A scandal spreads by word of mouth quickly.
He is a person who became famous through a scandal.

explain: '스캔들이 나다', '스캔들에 휘말리다'처럼 말해요. 뉴스나 글에서는 '추문'이라는 어려운 말도 있어요.
explain_en: People say 'seukaendeuri nada' (a scandal breaks out) and 'seukaendeure hwimallida' (get caught up in a scandal). In news and writing, a harder word, 'chumun', also exists.

examples.en: Containers are stacked high at the port.
They loaded the container onto the ship.
We are using a container box as an office.
I put the food in a small container.
I went to a cafe made from a shipping container.
Shipping containers have set sizes.

explain: 배나 트럭에 싣는 큰 상자와 음식을 담는 작은 용기 두 가지에 써요. 음식 용기는 '밀폐 용기'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It covers both the big box loaded on ships and trucks and a small food container. The food one is also called 'milpye yonggi'.

examples.en: The ball got caught in the net.
I hit the ball over the net.
A volleyball net is higher than you think.
The net is low, so the ball goes over easily.
In table tennis, the ball must go over the net.
The players set up the net before the match.

explain: 테니스, 배구, 탁구처럼 공을 넘기는 운동에 쓰는 말이에요. 물고기를 잡는 것은 '그물'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used in sports where the ball goes over a divider, such as tennis, volleyball, and table tennis. The net for catching fish is called 'geumul'.

examples.en: The speaker is too loud.
I played music through the speaker.
I bought a new Bluetooth speaker.

examples.ko: 스피커가 고장 났는지 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: The speaker seems broken, since there is no sound.
I connect my phone to the speaker.

examples.ko: 스피커는 방 구석에 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is better to put the speaker in a corner of the room.

explain: '스피커폰으로 통화하다'처럼 전화 소리를 밖으로 내는 기능에도 써요. 이어폰은 귀에 꽂고, 스피커는 밖으로 소리를 내요.
explain_en: It is also used for the phone function that plays call sound aloud, as in 'seupikeophoneuro tonghwahada'. Earphones go in your ears; a speaker sends sound out into the room.

examples.en: The thug in the movie came into the shop.
That person talks like a thug.
Many people are afraid of thugs.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 깡패에게 돈을 뺏겼어요.
examples.en: As a child, a local thug took my money.

examples.ko: 골목에서 깡패 같은 사람들을 만나서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: I met some thug-like people in an alley and was scared.
Please do not act like a thug.

explain: 사람에게 직접 '깡패 같다'고 하면 아주 심한 말이 될 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '불량배'가 있는데, 그건 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 나와요.
explain_en: Telling someone directly 'you are like a kkangpae' can be a harsh insult. A similar word is 'bullyangbae', which mostly appears in writing and the news.

examples.en: Teaching children is rewarding.
The volunteer work was a truly rewarding time.
I want to spend my day in a worthwhile way.
It was hard, but it was rewarding.
I found a rewarding and fun job.
If it is worthwhile work, I will see it through.

explain: '보람 있다'와 거의 같게 써요. '보람이 있어요', '보람을 느껴요'처럼 명사 '보람'으로도 많이 말해요. 자기 노력에 대한 만족을 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It works almost the same as 'boram itda'. People also use the noun: 'borami isseoyo' and 'borameul neukkyeoyo'. It suits satisfaction about your own effort.

examples.en: I do the sketch first and then add color.
The sketch is so simple that I cannot tell what it is.
I drew a few sketches in my notebook.
I do the sketch lightly with a pencil.
I will add color to this sketch.
I will show you a sketch first.

explain: '밑그림'은 색을 칠하기 전에 밑바탕으로 그리는 그림이고, '스케치'는 대상을 보고 빠르게 그린 그림 자체에도 써요. '여행 스케치'처럼 가볍게 그린 그림 이름으로도 붙어요.
explain_en: A '밑그림' is the underdrawing made before adding color, while '스케치' can also be a quick drawing of something you see, kept as a piece in itself. It also appears in names like '여행 스케치' for lightly drawn pictures.

examples.en: I sketch trees in the park.
Yesterday I sketched the sea.
It rained while I was sketching.
A pencil is handy when you sketch.
I want to sketch my friend's face.
After sketching, I will add color.

explain: '그림을 그리다'보다 가볍게 대강 그린다는 느낌이에요. 보통 '풍경을 스케치하다'처럼 그리는 대상을 목적어로 써요.
explain_en: It feels lighter than 'geurimeul geurida': a quick, rough drawing. The thing you draw is usually the object, as in 'punggyeongeul seukechihada'.

examples.en: The weather agency forecast rain for tomorrow.
The broadcast is forecasting a typhoon.
They forecast snow for the weekend.
The weather turned cloudy as forecast.
They will forecast that tomorrow will be clear.
The weather report did not forecast rain.

explain: 주로 기상청이나 방송이 주어예요. 일상 대화에서는 '내일 비 온대요'처럼 전해 들은 말로 날씨를 말해요.
explain_en: The subject is usually the weather agency or a broadcaster. In daily talk people say 'naeil bi ondaeyo' (I hear it will rain tomorrow) instead.

examples.en: A shirt collar is hard to iron.

examples.ko: 칼라 있는 옷을 입고 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview in clothes with a collar.
You look cool when you stand up the collar.
This coat has a big collar.
The collar got dirty, so I washed it.
I buttoned it all the way up to the collar.

explain: '컬러'(색)와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈려요. 옷의 목 부분은 '칼라', 색은 '컬러'라고 써요.
explain_en: It sounds close to 'keolleo' (color), which causes mix-ups. The neck part of clothing is 'kalla'; color is 'keolleo'.

examples.ko: 아이가 망토를 두르고 영웅 놀이를 해요.
examples.en: The child wears a cape and plays hero.
The cape fluttered in the wind.
In winter, a single cloak keeps me warm.
The black cloak has a hood attached.
You wear a cape draped over your shoulders.
I dressed up in a red cape.

explain: '빨간 망토'는 동화 제목으로도 유명해요. 겨울 외투는 보통 '코트'나 '외투'라고 하고, 망토는 만화나 옷 입기 놀이에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 'Ppalgan mangto' (Little Red Riding Hood) is a famous fairy-tale title. A winter outer garment is usually a 'coat' or 'oetu'; mangto shows up in comics and dress-up play.

examples.en: The baby gives mom a kiss on the cheek.
The child gave a kiss as a greeting.
If you want to give a kiss, ask first.
My puppy likes giving kisses on my face.
Grandma smiles every time I give her a kiss.
I give my child a kiss before bed.

explain: '키스하다'보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이라 아이, 가족, 연인 사이에 써요. 명사 '뽀뽀'를 써서 '뽀뽀를 하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is lighter and cuter than 'kiseuhada', and is used with children, family, and couples. You can also use the noun: 'ppopporeul hada'.

examples.en: The company became a sponsor of the competition.
We could not find a sponsor, so the event was scaled down.

examples.ko: 스폰서 덕분에 무료로 열 수 있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the sponsor, we could hold it for free.

examples.ko: 이 팀의 스폰서는 유명한 음료 회사예요.
examples.en: This team's sponsor is a famous beverage company.
We passed on our thanks to the sponsor.
We signed a contract with a new sponsor.

explain: '후원자', '후원하다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 방송이나 행사에서는 '협찬'이라는 말도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 'Huwonja' and 'huwonhada' are used too. In broadcasts and events you also see the word 'hyeopchan'.

examples.en: The princess wore a sparkling crown.
The crown looks too heavy.
The crown was decorated with gold and jewels.
There were many people in front of the crown at the museum.
Jewels are set in the crown.
She received a crown and prize money at the pageant.

explain: 머리에 쓰니까 '왕관을 쓰다'라고 해요. 왕의 자리 자체는 '왕위'나 '왕좌'라고 불러서 물건인 '왕관'과 구분해요.
explain_en: Because it sits on the head, you say '왕관을 쓰다'. The position of king itself is '왕위' or '왕좌', which is separate from the object, the '왕관'.
